newsitem.title: USA: Clinton and businessmen to discuss welfare Friday.
newsitem.headline: Clinton and businessmen to discuss welfare Friday.

text.p: President Bill Clinton plans to meet with businessmen on Friday to put a spotlight on his efforts to encourage companies to hire people on welfare, the White House said on Tuesday.

Since he signed welfare reform legislation into law in August, Clinton has often exhorted companies to hire welfare recipients. White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton was likely to make the argument again on Friday.

"This will be an opportutity I think to put a spotlight on those things that the president is doing and those things the president wants others to do to make welfare reform a success," McCurry said in his daily briefing.
"The private sector has to be a part of the effort to successfully implement welfare reform," McCurry added. "There have to be jobs there as we move welfare-dependant mothers off welfare into work."

Despite the objections of many liberals, Clinton signed into law a reform package that ends a 61-year federal guarantee of aid to the poor. The measure gives states broad power to design their own programs and places time limits on giving such assistance to individuals.
